claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

Let's start: **How many children are you looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! I'm looking to claim for my child Alex, who is 8 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! It's great to meet you, and I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.

Let me ask you a few more questions:

**Are you responsible for Alex? This means Alex lives with you, or you contribute to the cost of looking after them at least the same amount as Child Benefit would provide (currently £25.60 a week for an eldest or only child).**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives with me at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you for confirming that Alex lives with you.

**Is Alex a British citizen, or do they have the right to live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex is a British citizen.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent, thank you.

**Do you live in the UK?** (This includes England, Scotland, Wales, and Northern Ireland.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in England - in Manchester.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that.

**Is Alex currently in any of the following situations:**
- In hospital
- In residential care (such as a children's home)
- Living with someone else (for example, with another family member or in foster care)
- In local authority or other public care

Or does Alex live with you at home full-time?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex lives with me at home most of the time, but they were in a children's home for a couple of months recently.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know. I'd like to understand Alex's situation a bit better.

**Is Alex still spending any time in the children's home now, or have they returned to live with you full-time?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: They've returned to live with me full-time now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful to know, thank you.

Just to confirm one more thing: **While Alex was in the children's home, was the placement funded by a local authority (council), or did you pay for it privately yourself?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: It was a local authority placement - the council arranged it.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that.

One more question about that period: **How long was Alex in the local authority care placement? Was it more or less than 8 weeks in total?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: It was exactly 8 weeks.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that detail. Let me just check one more thing:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex, or has anyone else claimed Child Benefit for Alex recently?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for your patience. I now have all the information I need to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Based on what you've told me:

- Alex is 8 years old (under 16) ✓
- Alex is a British citizen ✓
- You live in the UK (England) ✓
- Alex lives with you and you are responsible for them ✓
- Alex was in local authority care for exactly 8 weeks, but has now returned to live with you full-time ✓
- No one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex ✓

Regarding the care placement: According to the rules, Child Benefit payments are affected if a child goes into care for **more than 8 weeks**. Since Alex was in care for exactly 8 weeks (not more than 8 weeks), and has now returned to live with you full-time, this should not affect your eligibility.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great news! Based on the information you've provided, **you are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's a summary of why:

**For Alex (age 8):** ✅ Eligible
- Alex is under 16 years old
- You live in the UK
- Alex is a British citizen with the right to live in the UK
- You are responsible for Alex as they live with you
- The local authority care placement was exactly 8 weeks, which does not exceed the threshold that would affect your eligibility (the rules specify that payments are only affected if care exceeds 8 weeks)
- Alex has now returned to live with you full-time
- No one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex

You should be able to make a claim for Child Benefit. If you haven't already claimed, you can do so through the official government channels. Is there anything else you'd like to know?
